nodes.summary: For binary trees $L$, $R$ and a key $k$, write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a tree $t$, $w(t) = |t| + 1$ for its weight, $w = w(L) + w(R)$, and $\langle X, x, Y \rangle$ for the node with key $x$, left subtree $X$ and right subtree $Y$. The rebalanced node $\mathrm{balance}(L, k, R)$ is defined as follows. If $3w < 4\,w(L)$, then $L = \langle A, a, B \rangle$ is a node; if $|B| \le 2|A|$, the result is the…
nodes.title: Weight-balanced rebalancing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $R$ be weight-balanced trees and $k$ a key, and write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a tree $t$. If $4(|L| + 1) \le 3(|L| + |R| + 2) + 1$ and $4(|R| + 1) \le 3(|L| + |R| + 2) + 1$, then the rebalanced node $\mathrm{balance}(L, k, R)$ is weight-balanced.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced rebalancing restores balance

nodes.summary: For every list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, the tree obtained from the empty tree by inserting $x_n, x_{n-1}, \dots, x_1$ in this order with weight-balanced insertion is weight-balanced.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced trees built by insertion are balanced

nodes.summary: For every key $x$ of a linearly ordered type and every weight-balanced tree $t$, the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $t$ with weight-balanced insertion is weight-balanced.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced insertion preserves balance

nodes.summary: Write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a tree $t$ and $w(t) = |t| + 1$ for its weight. Let $N$ be the node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$. Then $N$ is weight-balanced if and only if $L$ and $R$ are weight-balanced, $4\,w(L) \le 3\,w(N)$ and $4\,w(R) \le 3\,w(N)$. This is the classical $\mathrm{BB}[1/4]$ invariant: each child has weight at most three quarters of the weight of the node.
nodes.title: Weight form of the balance condition at a node

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $R$ be weight-balanced trees and $k$ a key, and write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a tree $t$. If $4(|L| + 1) \le 3(|L| + |R| + 2)$ and $4(|R| + 1) \le 3(|L| + |R| + 2)$, then the node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is weight-balanced.
nodes.title: Building a weight-balanced node

nodes.summary: Write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a binary tree $t$ and $w(t) = |t| + 1$ for its weight. A binary tree is weight-balanced, or satisfies the invariant $\mathrm{BB}[1/4]$, when it is empty, or when it is a node with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ such that $L$ and $R$ are weight-balanced, $4\,w(L) \le 3(w(L) + w(R))$ and $4\,w(R) \le 3(w(L) + w(R))$. Since the weight of a node is $w(L) + w(R)$, this says…
nodes.title: Weight-balanced trees

nodes.summary: The tree built from a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of elements of a linearly ordered type is obtained from the empty tree by inserting $x_n, x_{n-1}, \dots, x_1$ in this order with weight-balanced insertion; the empty list gives the empty tree.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced tree from a list

nodes.summary: Write $|t|$ for the number of keys of a binary tree $t$ and $h(t)$ for its height, where the empty tree has height $0$ and a node has height one more than the larger height of its two subtrees. If $t$ is weight-balanced, then $h(t) \le \lfloor \log_2 ((|t| + 1)^3) \rfloor + 1$.
nodes.title: Height of a weight-balanced tree is logarithmic

nodes.summary: For a key $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the insertion $\mathrm{insert}(x, t)$ of $x$ into a binary tree $t$ is defined by recursion on $t$. Into the empty tree it gives the single node with key $x$. Into the node $N$ with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ it gives $\mathrm{balance}(\mathrm{insert}(x, L), k, R)$ if $x < k$, $\mathrm{balance}(L, k, \mathrm{insert}(x, R))$ if $k < x$, and $N$ itself if…
nodes.title: Weight-balanced insertion

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order. For every key $x$ and every binary tree $t$, the number of nodes of $t$ is at most the number of nodes of the tree obtained from $t$ by weight-balanced insertion of $x$.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced insertion does not decrease the number of keys

nodes.summary: For binary trees $l$ and $r$ and a key $k$, an element $x$ occurs in the weight-balanced rebalancing of $l$, $k$, $r$ exactly when $x$ occurs in $l$, $x = k$, or $x$ occurs in $r$. Membership is structural: $x$ is the key of some node.
nodes.title: Membership after weight-balanced rebalancing

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order. For every key $x$ and every list $xs$, $x$ occurs in the weight-balanced tree built from $xs$ by repeated insertion exactly when $x$ is an element of $xs$.
nodes.title: Membership in a weight-balanced tree built from a list

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order. For all keys $x$, $y$ and every binary tree $t$, $y$ occurs in the tree obtained from $t$ by weight-balanced insertion of $x$ exactly when $y = x$ or $y$ occurs in $t$.
nodes.title: Membership after weight-balanced insertion

nodes.summary: Write $|t|$ for the number of nodes of a binary tree $t$. For binary trees $l$ and $r$ and a key $k$, the weight-balanced rebalancing of $l$, $k$, $r$ has exactly $|l| + |r| + 1$ nodes.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced rebalancing preserves the number of keys

nodes.summary: The empty binary tree has $0$ nodes.
nodes.title: Number of keys of the empty tree

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order. For every key $x$ and every binary tree $t$, the tree obtained from $t$ by weight-balanced insertion of $x$ has at most one more node than $t$.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced insertion adds at most one key

nodes.summary: Write $|t|$ for the number of nodes of a binary tree $t$. For binary trees $l$ and $r$ and a key $k$, the node with key $k$, left subtree $l$ and right subtree $r$ has $|l| + |r| + 1$ nodes.
nodes.title: Number of keys of a node

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order, let $l$ and $r$ be ordered binary trees (strict binary search trees), and let $k$ be a key such that every key of $l$ is less than $k$ and every key of $r$ is greater than $k$. Then the weight-balanced rebalancing of $l$, $k$, $r$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced rebalancing preserves ordering

nodes.summary: Let the keys carry a linear order. For every list $xs$, the weight-balanced tree built from $xs$ by repeated insertion is ordered, that is, a strict binary search tree.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced trees built from a list are ordered

nodes.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered. If a binary tree $t$ is ordered as a search tree (at every node, every key of the left subtree is strictly smaller and every key of the right subtree strictly larger than the key at the node), then the tree obtained from $t$ by weight-balanced insertion of any key $x$ is again ordered.
nodes.title: Weight-balanced insertion preserves the search-tree order

nodes.summary: Write $w(t)$ for the weight of a binary tree $t$ (its number of keys plus one), and measure height so that the empty tree has height $0$ and a node has height one more than the taller of its children. If $t$ is weight balanced with parameter $1/4$ (at every node, each child has weight at most three quarters of the weight of the node) and has height $k + 1$ for a natural number $k$, then $w(t) \ge (4/3)^k$; in…
nodes.title: Exponential weight lower bound for weight-balanced trees

nodes.summary: The Nievergelt–Reingold weight $w(t)$ of a binary tree $t$ is its number of keys plus one. Equivalently, it counts the external leaves: the empty tree has weight $1$, and the weight of a node is the sum of the weights of its two children.
nodes.title: Weight of a binary tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
